challengeData.heading: The cost of learning without a strategy.
challengeData.description: When there is no operating model behind L&D, training scatters: courses nobody asked for, no shared language for skills, and no way to prove impact.

stat.label: of L&D budgets are lost to training that is not tied to business priorities.

cards.title: No shared language

cards.title: Reactive, not planned
cards.description: L&D fields requests as they land, instead of building the capability the strategy needs next.

cards.title: Spend without direction
cards.description: Budgets fund requests, not priorities, so the gaps that matter to the business stay open.

cards.title: Learning that doesn't stick
cards.description: Programs run once and fade without reinforcement, so the same gaps reopen within a year.

cards.title: Nothing scales
cards.description: What works for one team can't be repeated across the org, so growth stalls.

cards.title: Nothing to measure
cards.description: With no framework, leaders cannot see whether learning changed performance or the bottom line.

blueprintData.heading: The Edstellar learning strategy blueprint.
blueprintData.description: Five connected layers that turn business strategy into a running learning function, and the model every engagement builds.

layers.title: Business alignment
layers.summary: The foundation every layer above is built on.
layers.description: We translate the business plan into the capabilities it demands. Get this wrong and every layer above it, the competency model, the curriculum, the metrics, is built for skills the business does not need.

layers.title: Capability model
layers.summary: The shared language everything above it is organized around.
layers.description: Built from the priorities in layer 01, it becomes the common language the operating model, the curriculum and the metrics all reference. Without it, none of them are comparable across the business.

layers.title: Operating model
layers.summary: What turns the model into a function that runs.
layers.description: A capability model is only a framework until someone owns it, funds it and governs it. This layer supplies the ownership and resourcing that let the architecture above it actually ship.

layers.title: Learning architecture
layers.summary: Where the strategy becomes what people actually learn.
layers.description: Pathways are mapped to the capability model in layer 02 and resourced by the operating model in layer 03. This is the point where the framework turns into programs a person can enroll in.

layers.title: Measurement
layers.summary: Closes the loop back to the business goals.
layers.description: Baselines are set against the capability model and read back against the business goals in layer 01. Without the four layers beneath it, there is nothing solid to measure or improve.

items.question: What does learning strategy and design consulting include?
items.answer: It covers your L&D operating model, capability and competency frameworks, curriculum architecture, learning measurement and governance, all aligned to the business plan.

items.question: How is a learning strategy different from a training plan?
items.answer: A training plan lists courses. A learning strategy defines the operating model, capability priorities and measurement that decide which courses matter and why, so spend follows business goals.

items.question: How long does a learning strategy engagement take?
items.answer: Typically four to eight weeks for the strategy and architecture, depending on organization size and how many roles are in scope.

items.question: Do you build the competency frameworks too?
items.answer: Yes. Role-based competency models and career pathways are a core deliverable, so capability is defined the same way across the business.

items.question: What do we get at the end?
items.answer: A business-aligned L&D strategy, a 12 to 24 month roadmap, competency frameworks, a curriculum blueprint and a measurement framework you own and run.
